item.title: #3591482: Language-neutral content ("und") counts as a template language – Summit is installed in "und" and every page fails
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591482 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

Installing Drupal CMS in a language other than English (e.g. German) with the Summit site template previously broke every page with a 500 error. The installer mistakenly treated "language not specified" (und) content as if it were a real language, which caused the site's default language configuration to be set to the invalid value und instead of the language actually chosen during installation. This made the Event Horizon theme crash immediately because it could not construct a number formatter for a non-existent und locale. The fix ignores these internal placeholder langcodes when the installer inspects a template's content, so the language picked during installation is respected.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Database update:
  • Config change: Fixes a bug where system.site:default_langcode and config_language_lock.locked_langcode could be incorrectly set to und (language-neutral) instead of the language chosen in the installer.

Technical details

SiteTemplate::getLangcodesFromContent() builds the list of langcodes present in a recipe's shipped content by scanning each content item's _meta.default_langcode and its translations keys. Summit ships 53 entities with default_langcode: en and 3 with no langcode at all, which Drupal represents internally as LanguageInterface::LANGCODE_NOT_SPECIFIED (und). Because that method previously returned ['en', 'und'], detectLanguages() saw two distinct langcodes and concluded the recipe is genuinely multilingual, triggering detectDefaultLangcode(), which simply returns the first default_langcode it encounters in content order. That value happened to be und, which got written into system.site:default_langcode and config_language_lock.locked_langcode, overriding the language actually selected in the installer.

The fix filters LanguageInterface::LANGCODE_NOT_SPECIFIED (und) and LANGCODE_NOT_APPLICABLE (zxx) out of the langcode list via array_diff() before deduplicating with array_unique(). With those placeholders removed, Summit's content now resolves to a single real langcode (en), so detectLanguages() treats it as monolingual and returns an empty array instead of forcing a default language, letting the installer's own language choice stand. detectDefaultLangcode() itself is unchanged; it no longer gets invoked in this scenario because the content no longer looks multilingual.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

item.title: #3591474: canvas_translate dependency in Drupal CMS 1.2 prevents auto updates
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591474 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

New sites built from Drupal CMS 1.2's Starter template showed a long composer warning whenever an automatic update was attempted, because the canvas_translate module (needed by the Multilingual recipe) was being pulled in only as an indirect dependency at an unstable (alpha) release, which Composer flags. The fix adds canvas_translate explicitly to the project's composer.json so its alpha stability is declared up front, and automatic updates proceed cleanly on new installs.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The Multilingual recipe (recipes/drupal_cms_multilingual/recipe.yml) installs the canvas_translate module, but project_template/composer.json never listed it as a top-level requirement, so Composer had to resolve it transitively. Since drupal/canvas_translate currently has no stable release, and the project sets "minimum-stability": "dev" with "prefer-stable": true, an unpinned transitive dependency at alpha stability produced the stability/update warning users saw when Drupal CMS's automatic update tooling ran composer under the hood.

The fix is a one-line addition to project_template/composer.json's require section: "drupal/canvas_translate": "@alpha". Declaring the package explicitly with its stability flag lets Composer resolve it deterministically without flagging the ambiguity, so sites scaffolded from the template (including via the graphical installer with the Starter recipe) no longer hit the warning on update.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

item.title: #3591472: Fresh 2.2.0 projects cannot composer require anything: recipe unpacking drops the @alpha flag on drupal/canvas_translate
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591472 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Any site built from composer create-project drupal/cms on version 2.2.0 was left in a broken state where adding or updating any Composer package afterward failed outright, with an error about drupal/canvas_translate being fixed to an alpha version that violates the project's minimum stability. This happened because Composer's recipe unpacking step, which runs at the end of create-project, merged two version constraints for drupal/canvas_translate (one from the root project, one from the bundled multilingual recipe) in a way that silently dropped the @alpha stability flag, while the lock file still pinned the actual alpha release. The fix restores that flag so freshly created projects can have modules added to them normally.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The root cause is in Composer's drupal/core-recipe-unpack package: Unpacker.php's call to SemVer::minimizeConstraints() merges the project template's "drupal/canvas_translate": "@alpha" with the drupal_cms_multilingual recipe's "drupal/canvas_translate": "^1" into a plain ^1, losing the stability flag even though composer.json still declares minimum-stability: stable and composer.lock keeps the actual 1.0.0-alpha4 version. Any later partial update (i.e. any composer require) then rejects the locked alpha version against the project's stability settings.

Rather than changing core's unpacker, the fix (commit 1b10389, "Make a stability affordance for canvas_translate") re-adds "drupal/canvas_translate": "@alpha" directly to project_template/composer.json, ensuring the root constraint always carries the stability flag on its own. A companion fix in the related issue #3591473 also changed the drupal_cms_multilingual recipe's own constraint from "^1" to "^1@alpha" in recipes/drupal_cms_multilingual/composer.json, so both sides of the merge already carry the alpha flag and minimizeConstraints() no longer has a way to drop it.

Upgrade

Sites already created from Drupal CMS 2.2.0 that hit this need to manually restore the stability flag in their project's root composer.json before requiring anything else:

"require": {
    "drupal/canvas_translate": "@alpha"
}

Alternatively, avoid triggering the bug on new projects with the documented workaround: composer create-project --no-install drupal/cms test-site, then cd test-site && composer install. This keeps recipes packed (rather than unpacked) so the @alpha flag in composer.json is never dropped, and later composer require calls work normally.

Contribution

item.title: #3591433: Add a drupal_cms_multilingual recipe with content translation features
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591433 · 1 contributor · 23 comments

Summary

Drupal CMS now offers a "Multilingual" recipe (drupal_cms_multilingual) that site owners can apply to add multi-language support to their site. Applying it installs Drupal core's Language, Content Translation, Interface Translation and Configuration Translation modules, along with the contributed Better Content Language Settings, Canvas Translate and Language Checklist modules. After applying the recipe, the site gains a "Multilingual setup checklist" page (under Administration » Configuration » Regional and language) that walks the owner through adding languages, choosing how the site detects a visitor's language, marking which content types and fields are translatable, and translating content, configuration and the admin interface.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New drupal_cms_multilingual recipe installs Language, Content Translation, Interface Translation, Configuration Translation plus the Better Content Language Settings, Canvas Translate and Language Checklist contributed modules.

Technical details

The recipe lives at recipes/drupal_cms_multilingual and is a plain recipe.yml that lists the modules to install (better_content_language_settings, canvas_translate, config_translation, content_translation, language, language_checklist, locale) and imports the language.entity.und and language.entity.zxx config entities, which are needed so that adding a language on the Languages page does not crash (recipes do not automatically bring in the config entities of the modules they install). It also declares a Project Browser task pointing at the checklistapi.checklists.language_checklist route, so the checklist shows up as a "Finish multilingual setup" follow-up action.

The recipe is wired into drupal_cms_starter's recommended.yml as a suggested add-on and into the project_template/composer.json as a ^2 dependency, so new Drupal CMS installs can pick it up as one of the recommended recipes. Its functional test, ComponentValidationTest, applies the recipe against sites installed in English or Hungarian, with and without Config Language Lock, and verifies it is idempotent, preserves the install language as the default, and that its follow-up Project Browser task resolves to a working page.

item.title: #3591466: Installing in another language does not translate shipped configuration: the installer dropped core's config translation step accidentally
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Critical bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591466 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

Installing Drupal CMS in a language other than English silently stopped translating the configuration that ships with modules and site templates (things like view titles). A recent optimization to speed up installation accidentally dropped the step that actually applies downloaded translations to configuration, even though the language itself was still set up correctly. This fix restores that step, so installing in German or any other supported language now produces a fully translated site again, as it did before the regression.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The regression was introduced when drupal_cms_installer_finish_translations() (added for #3591422 to lock configuration language and speed up install) replaced core's install_finish_translations() batch. That change kept the langcode-locking batch from ConfigLanguageLockBatch but dropped the actual translation-rewrite batch that core's original function ran via Locale\LocaleConfigBatch. As a result, .po translations were still downloaded and language settings were locked, but the translated strings were never written into shipped configuration, leaving locales_location empty for configuration and shipped config, such as the content view's label, untranslated.

The fix adds back a call to LocaleConfigBatch::buildBatch() after the config language lock batch in drupal_cms_installer.profile, so the sequence is now: download translation files, lock/rewrite config langcodes via ConfigLanguageLockBatch, then rewrite config content with translations via LocaleConfigBatch, mirroring core's original two-step process but with the langcode-locking behavior config_language_lock provides. Test coverage was added to TranslatedInstallTest asserting that the content view's label is translated after a German install, guarding against this regression recurring. The workaround is expected to be removed once core issue #3337864 is resolved.

Contribution

item.title: #3591452: Site template with multilingual demo content only works if its intended default language is chosen by the user beforehand, otherwise breaks Canvas
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591452 · 1 contributor · 10 comments

Summary

Drupal CMS site templates that ship demo content in more than one language (for example English content with Spanish translations) could silently break Canvas, because the installer lets people pick any language before they pick a template. Depending on which language was chosen during install, the original English content could be discarded instead of kept as a translation, and in some cases none of the shipped content matched the site's configured default language at all, leaving Canvas broken. Site templates can now declare which languages their demo content is shipped in and which of those is the intended default. If the language chosen during install is one the template supports, the installer imports as before but keeps the original values as a translation instead of throwing them away. If the chosen language is not one the template supports, the installer installs the site in the template's own default language so the demo content imports correctly, then adds the user's originally chosen language to the site afterwards. Templates that don't declare any languages behave exactly as before.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New optional languages key (default, available) under extra.drupal_cms_installer in a site template's recipe.yml, letting it declare which languages its demo content ships in.

Technical details

Site templates can now declare a languages key under extra.drupal_cms_installer in recipe.yml, with default (the template's own default content language) and available (all languages it ships translations for). The Drupal CMS installer tracks this as a LanguagePlan value object and exposes it via a languages property on SiteTemplate, re-applying it on every installer request since core re-derives the runtime default language from the langcode URL parameter each time.

When the user's chosen installer language is in the template's available list, the install proceeds in that language as before, but the installer now asks core to keep English (keep_english) when needed and an event subscriber preserves the original shipped values as a translation whenever core's DefaultContent\Importer swaps content into the chosen default language, so nothing shipped by the template is lost. This addresses a gap in core's own Importer::verifyNormalizedLanguage() behavior, described in the issue as a polyfill pending a core fix. When the chosen language isn't one the template supports, the installer instead sets the site default language to the template's declared default before recipes run, so demo content imports exactly as shipped, and adds the user's originally chosen language to the site afterwards. The configuration language lock follows the site default language (the template's default in this case), while the administrator account still gets the user's originally chosen language as its preferred language.

Upgrade

Site templates that ship demo content in multiple languages should declare this in recipe.yml:

extra:
  drupal_cms_installer:
    languages:
      default: en
      available:
        - en
        - es

A template must ship a language.entity.* config entity for every language listed in available, including the declared default. Templates that don't add this key are unaffected and keep working exactly as before.

item.title: #3591440: Fix installer page backgrounds and add interstitial at the end
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591440 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The Drupal CMS installer used to leave the final progress bar sitting at 100% for several seconds (uninstalling the install profile, rebuilding the router, flushing caches) with no feedback, which looked like the install had stalled or that the last visible step (often translation import) was slow. A new "Your site is almost ready" holding screen with a spinner now displays during that final cleanup so the wait reads as intentional. At the same time, the decorative background artwork that previously only appeared on a few installer forms has been extended to the batch/progress screens (including the module installation step, which now uses a previously unused "recipes" pattern), so the whole install experience looks visually consistent instead of switching between patterned forms and bare white progress pages.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In drupal_cms_installer.profile, drupal_cms_installer_install_tasks_alter() now inserts a new install task, drupal_cms_installer_almost_ready, immediately before install_finished (using the module's existing $insert_before helper). That task renders a holding page (cms-installer__finishing markup with heading, subhead, and CSS spinner) and attaches a Refresh meta tag pointing back to install.php with the original install parameters, so the page displays for one render cycle and then the browser auto-refreshes into the real install_finished step.

The per-step decorative artwork was refactored from several separate hook_form_alter() implementations (each attaching its own #theme => step_svg element with a #weight) into a single lookup in drupal_cms_installer_theme_preprocess_install_page(). It reads $install_state['active_task'] and maps it via a match expression to a pattern id (settings, name, account, recipes, or none), exposing it as the pattern template variable. install-page.html.twig prints {{ pattern }} inside <main> after page.content, so the artwork now renders consistently across forms and batch/progress pages alike, instead of only on individual forms. New CSS (.cms-installer__finishing, .cms-installer__finishing-spinner, and a cms-installer-finishing keyframe animation with a prefers-reduced-motion fallback) styles the new interstitial, and .cms-installer__main .progress is capped at 720px so the progress bar aligns with the body copy above it now that batch screens carry the same artwork.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

item.title: #3489408: Enable filenames sanitization
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3489408 · 4 contributors · 9 comments
  • Followers: 4
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 4 contributors

Summary

Drupal CMS now enables Drupal core's filename sanitization for whitespace by default. Previously, uploading a file with spaces in its name (e.g. "my photo.jpg") left the spaces intact, which can cause SEO, readability, and URL-compatibility issues. Sites built with Drupal CMS's foundational recipe now automatically replace whitespace in uploaded filenames, without any manual configuration.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: Drupal CMS's base recipe (drupal_cms_site_template_base, formerly drupal_cms_content_type_base) now sets file.settings:filename_sanitization.replace_whitespace to true, so newly uploaded file names have spaces replaced with hyphens by default.

Technical details

Drupal core's file module has long supported filename sanitization via file.settings:filename_sanitization, with independent toggles for transliterate, replace_whitespace, replace_non_alphanumeric, deduplicate_separators, and lowercase (all false by default). Drupal CMS's base recipe now applies a simpleConfigUpdate action on file.settings that flips only filename_sanitization.replace_whitespace to true; the other sanitization options (transliteration of accented characters, non-alphanumeric replacement, lowercasing) remain off.

The setting currently lives in recipes/drupal_cms_site_template_base/recipe.yml, after that recipe absorbed the former drupal_cms_content_type_base recipe (where the setting originated) in a later reorganization. Because recipes apply configuration only at recipe-application time, this affects new sites (or existing sites that reapply the recipe); it does not retroactively rename already-uploaded files.

Contribution

Timeline

item.title: #3577804: The installer should set a state flag to remember what site template was applied
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3577804 · 1 contributor · 2 comments
  • Followers: 1
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 1 contributor

Summary

During Drupal CMS installation, when a user selects the "Blank" (starter kit) site template on the site template selection form, the installer now stores the chosen template's recipe locator in the site_template_base state key. This state flag is deliberately environment-local (state is never ported between environments) and is used by a new export endpoint that lets users with the administer site configuration permission download the current site as a recipe ZIP file from /admin/config/development/site-export. This lays the groundwork for future contextual guidance in the admin UI. This change was implemented as part of #3575283.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New @api route /admin/config/development/site-export for downloading the current site as a recipe ZIP, and site_template_base state key written during installation when the 'Blank' site template is selected.

Technical details

In SiteTemplateForm::submitForm(), a new StateInterface dependency is injected. When the submitted choice is drupal_cms_site_template_base, the recipe locator path is written to state via $this->state->set('site_template_base', $locator) before the recipe is enqueued. Only the "Blank" starter kit triggers this; other site templates (Haven, Byte, etc.) do not set the key.

The state key feeds the new ExportController::exportArchive() (an @internal controller in drupal_cms_helper), which calls SiteExporter::export($destination, $this->state()->get('site_template_base')). SiteExporter::export() was refactored to accept an optional ?string $base parameter: when a base path is provided and the directory exists, the new private copyBaseRecipe() method mirrors it to the destination (excluding content/) and renames any *.example files by stripping the suffix. When no base is set, the directory is prepared from scratch as before. The exporter also now deletes config/.htaccess from the output, since the exported recipe is meant to be shared.

A new route drupal_cms_helper.site_export at /admin/config/development/site-export is marked # @api in drupal_cms_helper.routing.yml. It requires the administer site configuration permission and a custom exportArchiveAccess() check that verifies PharData is available. The ExportController class itself carries the @internal marker; only the route path is part of the public API surface.

Drupal CMS is shipping its first real-world site template, aimed at SaaS and B2B product marketing websites. The template bundles an opinionated set of recipes, content types, layout components, and demo content so a site owner can spin up a product site with a blog, feature highlights, pricing section, FAQ, testimonials, and a contact form. The implementation ultimately landed as the separate byte project (drupal.org/project/byte) rather than inside the main Drupal CMS repository.

  • New API: New drupal_cms_b2b_template site recipe (now the byte project at drupal.org/project/byte) for bootstrapping SaaS and B2B product marketing sites on Drupal CMS.

The MR scaffolded a drupal/drupal_cms_b2b_template recipe (type: Site) requiring drupal/core ^11.2 and drupal/drupal_cms_blog ^2. The recipe.yml applied administrator_role, content_editor_role, and drupal_cms_blog as recipe dependencies, and imported system.menu.footer and system.menu.main config. The MR was closed without merging; the full implementation moved to the byte project.

The issue body defines the intended content model: Blog Post (delegated to drupal_cms_blog as a dependency rather than copied), Feature and FAQ content types as nodes (so editors find all content at /admin/content), and a Changelog page built on drupal_cms_page. item.description:

Summary

Drupal CMS now includes the navigation_extra_tools contributed module by default. This gives all Drupal CMS sites one-click links in the navigation toolbar to flush all caches, run cron, run database updates, and other common administrative operations. Previously, site builders had to navigate to Configuration > Development > Performance to clear caches, or install Admin Toolbar Extra Tools separately to get these shortcuts.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New navigation_extra_tools module bundled in the base Drupal CMS recipe, providing toolbar shortcuts to flush caches, run cron, and run updates on all Drupal CMS sites

Technical details

The navigation_extra_tools module (version ^1.3) was added to the install list in recipes/drupal_cms_site_template_base/recipe.yml and declared as a Composer dependency in recipes/drupal_cms_site_template_base/composer.json. Because drupal_cms_site_template_base is the foundational recipe applied to every Drupal CMS installation, these toolbar shortcuts are available on all Drupal CMS sites without any additional setup. The module integrates with core's Navigation module, which Drupal CMS already installs. The feature request was prompted by the observation that Drupal CMS does not assume Admin Toolbar is installed, leaving users without the quick-access admin links they were accustomed to from Admin Toolbar Extra Tools.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: January 24, 2025

Collaboration

The reporter, chike, noted that after switching to Drupal CMS they repeatedly had to navigate to Configuration > Development > Performance to flush caches because the familiar Admin Toolbar shortcuts were absent. A follow-up comment from thejimbirch pointed to the navigation_extra_tools module as the right solution. chike then specifically called for it to be bundled, describing it as "absolutely essential," which is the direct path to the fix recorded here.
